keyVerseText: And your father hath deceived me, and changed my wages ten times; but God suffered him not to hurt me.
rootMeaning: The root of מֹנֶה (môneh) is מָנָה (mânâh), which fundamentally means to weigh out or measure. This root conveys the idea of careful appointment or allotment, extending metaphorically to counting, numbering, or setting a portion. Thus, beyond the simple English gloss of 'times,' the root emphasizes a measured, deliberate allocation or appointment of moments or instances, highlighting the precision and intentionality behind the concept of time or number.
usageInScripture: The word מֹנֶה appears only twice in Scripture, and in both instances it is translated as 'times.' This consistency in translation suggests a focused semantic range centered on the idea of counted or measured intervals. The fact that it is used to describe repeated occurrences, such as tenfold changes, underscores its role in expressing quantifiable, discrete portions of time or number, rather than vague or indefinite durations.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מֹנֶה as a measured, appointed portion enriches our grasp of God's sovereignty over time and events. It reminds believers that moments in life are not random but are weighed and allotted by divine providence. This aligns with the biblical theme that God ordains times and seasons (Acts 1:7), reinforcing trust in His perfect timing and control. The concept also points to the faithfulness of God in sustaining His people through appointed trials and blessings, assuring believers that each 'time' serves a purpose within His redemptive plan centered in Christ.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 31:7, the phrase 'changed my wages ten times' uses מֹנֶה to express the repeated alterations in the speaker's compensation. The word highlights the exactness and frequency of these changes, emphasizing the magnitude of the injustice suffered. Yet, the verse also reveals God's protection despite these repeated trials, encouraging believers to trust that God governs even the most trying 'times' of life with sovereign care.
